title: Attention scheduler sim + profiling scribble
content:
Quick objective:
- Build a lightweight scheduler simulator to reproduce latency tails we see in staged workloads; correlate with kernel selection (FlashAttention vs paged vs fused kernels) and KV cache pressure.

Background/context (why this doc):
- Multiple teams have seen ∼5–15% 99th latency regressions in mixed small/large sequence workloads after the recent fused-op rollout.
- Production traces show a bimodal latency distribution; hypothesis: scheduler decisions + kernel warm-up + memory evictions create intermittent slow requests.
- Want an iterative notebook of experiments, not a polished report.

Top-level hypotheses to validate:
1) Small-batch coalescing sometimes forces paged-attn path which is slower for short sequences due to copy overheads.
2) Kernel fusion increases single-kernel runtime variance for mid-length tokens under certain occupancy regimes.
3) KV cache memory pressure + async prefetch timing causes occasional host->device stalls that propagate into 95–99th p99s.

Simulator design notes (toy scheduler):
- Input: trace of (seq_len, batch_id, arrival_ts). Using replay samples from prod-traces/2024-11 (anonymized).
- Workload shapes: 40% short(<=64), 40% mid(128-512), 20% long(>512).
- Scheduler policies: FIFO, batch-coalesce (time-window 2ms), latency-first (short priority), occupancy-aware (estimate GPU occupancy and split).
- Kernel choice model: probability rules based on coalesced batch size + seq length + model variant (quantized vs full).
- Prefetch model: prefetch triggered if predicted seq_len > 128 AND KV cache free pages > threshold; prefetch latency sampled from empirical distribution.

Profiling harness (how I run experiments):
- Build variants: fused-ops-on / fused-ops-off ; flash-paged-preference toggles.
- Tools: nsight compute + CUPTI traces for per-kernel occupancy; nvprof for quick runs; custom per-request timers in runtime.
- Commands used (examples):
  - ./run_trace_replay --trace samples/mixed-short-mid-2024-11.json --policy=batch-coalesce --kernel-hint=fused-on --out=logs/runA
  - nsight --session runA.nsc --collect=metrics:sm__throughput_avg,mem__throughput
  - python parse_trace.py logs/runA --percentiles 50 90 95 99 > logs/runA-summary.txt

Representative run notes (toy numbers; wall-clock ms):
- FIFO, fused-on: p50=6.2ms, p90=14.1ms, p95=20.5ms, p99=47.3ms
- batch-coalesce (2ms window), fused-on: p50=5.0ms, p90=12.8ms, p95=18.1ms, p99=72.9ms (wider tail)
- occupancy-aware, fused-off, prefer-flash: p50=6.8ms, p90=13.6ms, p95=19.9ms, p99=39.8ms

Observations / quick interpretation:
- Coalescing helps median/90 but can amplify p99 when it occasionally groups together a long seq with many small ones, triggering expensive kernel paths and spilling prefetch.
- Fused-op variant reduces median latency for large batches but shows higher variance at mid occupancy; nsight traces show occasional SM underutilization spikes (context switches/wavefront stalls).
- Prefetch pipeline: when prefetch kicked in concurrently with an unexpected long request, device->host syncs caused up to 30ms extra tail on affected requests.

Micro-profiling snippets (copied results):
- Kernel time breakdown (sample):
  - softmax-fused: avg 4.2ms, std 1.1ms (heavy tail when occupancy dip)
  - flash-attn-kernel: avg 2.8ms, std 0.5ms
  - paged-copy-overhead: avg 1.5ms, but spikes to 8–12ms when page faults triggered

Anomalies found in traces:
- A recurring 11:03UTC window where many requests experienced identical ~8ms delay; correlates with background consolidation job in Dedicated pool that triggered memory reclamation (ticket RWINF-2981).
- Rare spike where fused kernel launched but chose fallback to paged path mid-execution (race between kernel-launch heuristics and seq-length re-eval). Need to reproduce with synthetic trace.

Short checklist / experiments to run next:
- [ ] Add a deterministic seed mode to scheduler sim to reproduce rare grouping case (capture exact batch composition).
- [ ] Run an isolated workload with forced prefetch latency injection to quantify p99 sensitivity curve.
- [ ] Compare fused-op under two compiler flags (fast-math toggle) to see effect on variance.
- [ ] Add a lightweight probe to the runtime path to record kernel selection reason codes (heuristic id).

Questions / unknowns:
- How often in real traffic does the grouping that triggers paged fallbacks occur? (need sliding-window analysis on prod traces)
- Is there a safe conservative policy (e.g., prefer flash for short sequences even if small-batch) that avoids regressions for med/long tails?

Quick decisions proposed:
- Short-term: disable time-window coalescing for Dedicated tier while we run focused sim experiments. (Pros: reduces p99 spikes; Cons: med latency rises slightly).
- Medium-term: instrument selection heuristics and add a backoff for prefetch when device is above 70% occupancy.

Notes-to-self / loose TODOs:
- capture a nsight capture of the 2ms window coalescing run where p99 jumped (log id runA).
- loop in SRE: check if background consolidation jobs can be scheduled outside peak.

Links and references (internal):
- trace replay toolkit: github.com/redwood-inference/trace-replay
- recent convo on slack #serving-runtime: thread ts 1702xxxxxxx (see linked_artifacts)

End of scribble. Will refine into a short runbook once we have deterministic reproducer.
